title: Flat completion map at a finite separable closed point
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be fields, let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak p\subset S$ be maximal with residue field $F=S/\mathfrak p$ finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Fix a $k$-embedding $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$. Define $e:S\otimes_kK\to K$ by $e(s\otimes\lambda)=\iota(\bar s)\lambda$, $\mathfrak q=\ker(e)$, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue fields $F,K$, and the map $s\mapsto s\otimes1$ induces a flat local $k$-algebra map $g:A\to B$, $g(s/u)=(s\otimes1)/(u\otimes1)$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Moreover $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$ and $\dim A=\dim B$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $R=\widehat A=\varprojlim_r A/\mathfrak m^r$ and $C=\widehat B=\varprojlim_r B/\mathfrak n^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. These are Noetherian complete local rings [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak mR$, $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak nC$ and residue fields $F,K$. The map $g$ induces a continuous flat local $k$-algebra map $h:R\to C$, given at each level by $a\bmod\mathfrak m^r\mapsto g(a)\bmod\mathfrak n^r$, with $\mathfrak m_RC=\mathfrak m_C$ and residue map $\iota$. Let $\tau:K\to C$ be the structural map induced by $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. For every $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to R$ of the residue map, $h\circ\sigma=\tau\circ\iota$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), first two paragraphs and flat-completion paragraph; Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), 0C4Z (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-dim), 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified); More Algebra Tag 0C4G (lemma-flat-completion).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change] to the given $S,\mathfrak p,F,K,\iota$. Its evaluation map is exactly $e$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings, $g$ has the asserted fraction formula, and $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$ with $B/\mathfrak n=K$. Faithful flatness implies flatness by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. The residue field of $A$ is $F$: the maps $S/\mathfrak p\to A/\mathfrak m$ and $s/u\mapsto\bar s/\bar u$ are inverse, since $u\notin\mathfrak p$ means $\bar u\ne0$. The displayed evaluation formula on fractions therefore gives the residue map $F\to K$ as $\iota$. Both maps preserve the structural $k$-maps.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat) and 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified); evaluation at the selected embedding.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] for the flat map $g:A\to B$ and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, whose contraction is $\mathfrak m$ because $g$ is local. Localizing a local ring at its maximal ideal changes no elements: all denominators are already units. The formula thus reads $\dim B=\dim A+\dim(B/\mathfrak mB)$. The closed fibre is $K$ by Step 1, and a field has just the prime $(0)$, hence dimension zero. Consequently $\dim A=\dim B$.

source.place: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), applied to the two maximal ideals.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $R$ and $C$ are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], they are local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak mR$ and $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak nC$, and their residue fields identify with $A/\mathfrak m=F$ and $B/\mathfrak n=K$ by first projection. The ideals $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak n$ are finitely generated by the definition of Noetherianity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with module equal to its ring: $R$ is complete for the extended powers $\mathfrak m^rR=(\mathfrak mR)^r$, and $C$ for $\mathfrak n^rC=(\mathfrak nC)^r$. These power identities follow by expanding products of ideal generators. This is precisely completeness for their maximal ideals.

Since $g(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, it sends $\mathfrak m^r$ into $\mathfrak n^r$ for every $r\ge1$. The resulting quotient maps commute with reduction, so componentwise application defines a $k$-algebra homomorphism $h:R\to C$ on compatible sequences [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It satisfies $h\iota_A=\iota_Bg$ for the canonical completion maps. First projection gives $\pi_C h=\iota\pi_R$ by Step 1. Since $\pi_R,\pi_C$ have the respective maximal ideals as kernels and $\iota$ is injective, $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_R$, so $h$ is local. Define $\tau$ by $K\to S\otimes_kK\to B\to C$, $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$ followed by localization and completion; its residue is $\lambda$, since $e(1\otimes\lambda)=\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), first paragraph of proof; compatible quotient maps and structural K-map.

proof.text: The componentwise map of Step 4 is the completed map in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion]. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1: $g$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Hence $h$ is flat. Moreover $\mathfrak m_RC$ is generated by $h(\iota_A(a))=\iota_B(g(a))$ for $a\in\mathfrak m$: an arbitrary element of $\mathfrak mR$ is a finite sum of multiples of such $\iota_A(a)$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_RC=\mathfrak mC=(\mathfrak mB)C=\mathfrak nC=\mathfrak m_C$. For every $r$, $h(\mathfrak m_R^r)\subseteq\mathfrak m_C^r$, which proves continuity for the maximal-ideal adic topologies.

source.place: Tag 0C4G (lemma-flat-completion); varieties Tag 0C54, final flat-completion paragraph.

proof.text: The complete local ring $C$ of Step 3 is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] with ideal $\mathfrak m_C$. The finite separable extension $F/k$ is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] converts its affine-scheme statement into the étale ring map $k\to F$. Now apply [lem-sc-etale-henselian-ring-lift] with its $R=k$, $B=F$, $S=C$, field $K$, $\epsilon=\pi_C$, $\beta$ the structural map $k\to C$, and $\theta=\iota$. All hypotheses hold: $\pi_C$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak m_C$, and $\pi_C\beta$ is the given inclusion $k\to K$. For any section $\sigma$, the two $k$-algebra maps $h\sigma$ and $\tau\iota$ both reduce to $\iota$: $\pi_Ch\sigma=\iota\pi_R\sigma=\iota$ and $\pi_C\tau\iota=\iota$. Uniqueness in the cited lifting statement gives $h\circ\sigma=\tau\circ\iota$.

The statement is unchanged and there is no repair note. Source: Stacks 0C54 (varieties.tex line 4101 on), which builds the local map of completions and the coefficient square. I checked each step against its cited statements. S1: the evaluation-local-base-change node gives q maximal, A and B Noetherian local, and g faithfully flat (hence flat) and local with mB=n and B/n=K; A/m=F is elementary. S2: 00ON is applied at n over m; the fibre is K, so dim A=dim B. S3: 0316, 05GI/05GG and module completeness with m^nR=(mR)^n give R and C Noetherian, complete and local, with residue fields F and K. S4 is elementary: the componentwise h is local because pi_C h = iota pi_R; tau has residue map the identity. S5: the 0C4G node uses the same componentwise map, so h is flat; m_R C = (mB)C = m_C. S6: C is henselian by 0ALJ (matches def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology); k->F is étale by 00U3 via 02GJ; uniqueness in 08HQ with R=k, B=F, S=C, theta=iota gives h sigma = tau iota for every section sigma. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. Edge cases: S=F; k[t] at (t) with transcendental K; F[t]/(t^2). Inseparable F would break mB=n, so separability is genuinely used. The citer field-extension-completion-presentation Step 1 uses only clauses the item states. No SGA source is used. I accept the declared tool_uses: adic-completion-noetherian, flat-completion, complete-pair-henselian and sc-etale-henselian-ring-lift.
